title: Promises, query counts and practical claims
objectives: Compare exact deterministic and randomized classical queries.
Separate ideal query advantages from end-to-end computational performance.
prerequisites: Chapters 5–7: Hadamard interference, joint states, XOR oracle action, phase kickback and bit ordering.

quizzes.question: For k=5 independent uniform classical samples with replacement, what is the balanced-function misclassification probability?
feedback: Either all-zero or all-one sampled outputs can cause error.
The error decreases as more independent samples are taken.

quizzes.question: What does one ideal oracle query establish about practical running time?
options: It states an access count under an ideal model; implementation costs remain to be evaluated.
It means the oracle uses one elementary gate.
feedback: The complete resource costs and success assumptions matter.
Correct: query complexity and elapsed-time performance are distinct.
An oracle can require a large circuit.
